bugs.name: Dashboard info dialog stays hidden in fullscreen
bugs.summary: The More info control becomes ineffective in dashboard fullscreen mode because its dialog is not visible until fullscreen is closed.
bugs.expected: More info should display its dialog while the dashboard is in fullscreen mode.
bugs.actual: The More info control becomes ineffective in dashboard fullscreen mode because its dialog is not visible until fullscreen is closed.
reproSteps: Open a dashboard and enter fullscreen mode.
Select More info.
See no dialog in fullscreen, then exit fullscreen and see the dialog appear.

bugs.name: Product breakdown ignores the dashboard Product Category filter
bugs.summary: The Product breakdown card continues to show every category when the dashboard is filtered to one.
bugs.expected: The breakdown should reflect the selected Product Category or clearly indicate that it is unfiltered.
bugs.actual: With Gizmo selected and surrounding copy naming Gizmo, Product breakdown still shows Doohickey, Gadget, Gizmo, and Widget percentages.
reproSteps: Open E-commerce Insights > Portfolio Performance.
Set Product Category to Gizmo only.
Compare the filter chip and adjacent Gizmo chart with Product breakdown, which still lists all four categories.

bugs.name: Revenue per quarter title remains after switching to monthly grouping
bugs.summary: A dashboard card retains a quarterly title while showing monthly revenue and month-over-month comparison.
bugs.expected: The card title should reflect the selected Date Grouping.
bugs.actual: With Date Grouping set to Month, “Revenue per quarter” shows Sep 2026 and compares with the previous month.
reproSteps: Open E-commerce Insights on the Overview tab.
Set Date Grouping to Month.
Compare the Revenue per quarter title with its Sep 2026 and previous-month values.

bugs.name: Resetting an open Product Category filter leaves stale checked options
bugs.summary: Reset changes the applied dashboard filter but leaves the open checklist on its prior selection.
bugs.expected: The open options should update to the default selections when the filter is reset.
bugs.actual: After resetting a Widget-only filter, the chip shows four selections while the open list still checks only Widget and offers Update filter.
reproSteps: On E-commerce Insights > Portfolio Performance, select only Widget in Product Category and apply.
Reopen the Product Category list, then click the chip’s Reset filter to default state control without closing the list.
Compare the four-selection chip with the stale Widget-only checklist.

bugs.name: Wine-tasting reviews shown in E-commerce Insights customer survey responses
bugs.summary: Customer survey responses in the E-commerce Insights customer satisfaction section are wine/distillery reviews rather than feedback about the dashboard's displayed e-commerce products.
bugs.expected: The Customer survey responses table under Customer Satisfaction should show feedback relevant to products or purchases in this e-commerce dashboard.
bugs.actual: The stable table shows reviews mentioning peachy fruit and 12-year-old bottlings, the Legacy series, a distillery, and distilling. This is inconsistent with the surrounding dashboard, which identifies product categories as Doohickey, Gizmo, Gadget, and Widget and lists items such as a Copper Knife, Silk Chair, Wool Car, and Keyboard as best sellers.

Select the Portfolio Performance tab.
Scroll to Customer Satisfaction → Customer survey responses.
Read the Body column. Observe sample reviews discussing whisky bottlings, the Legacy series, and distilleries.
Compare the review content with the dashboard’s displayed products and categories: Doohickey, Gizmo, Gadget, and Widget.

bugs.name: Dashboard duplication silently drops external Link cards
bugs.summary: External Link cards are omitted from dashboard copies in both duplication modes. Fresh source6→copy7 testing with heading, text, iframe, and external link preserves all other card types but loses the link. Duplicating a tab preserves the link, isolating this to dashboard duplication.
bugs.expected: Dashboard duplication preserves external Link cards on their corresponding tabs, as tab duplication does.
bugs.actual: The copied dashboard retains tabs, headings, text, iframe and question cards but omits external Link cards. Edit mode confirms the link card is absent.
reproSteps: Sign in and create or open a test dashboard.
Enter Edit mode, choose Add a link or iframe > Link, enter https://example.com, and press Enter.
Save the dashboard and verify the link is visible on its tab. Reproduced sources include dashboard3 Details QA and dashboard6 Details QA.
Choose More > Duplicate, name the copy, and confirm Duplicate. Reproduced in both default full-copy mode and Only duplicate dashboard mode.
Open the corresponding tab on the copied dashboard.
Observe the external Link card is absent while other cards and the tab remain. Open Edit mode to confirm the card was omitted.
As a control, duplicate the source tab: its Link card is preserved.

bugs.name: Duplicating a dashboard re-enables disabled Auto-apply filters
bugs.summary: Both dashboard duplication modes lose the source dashboard's disabled Auto-apply filters setting, changing copied dashboards from manual Apply to immediate query execution. Verified source dashboard 3 retains disabled setting after fresh navigation, while copies 4 and 5 enable it.
bugs.expected: The duplicated dashboard preserves the source's saved Auto-apply filters setting and requires Apply when the source does.
bugs.actual: Both the full duplicate and 'Only duplicate dashboard' copy have Auto-apply filters enabled. Filter selection executes immediately in the copies, while the source stages changes until Apply.
reproSteps: Sign in and open a dashboard with a mapped filter, such as /dashboard/3-qa-dashboard-journeys.
Open the dashboard More menu, choose Edit settings, disable Auto-apply filters, and close settings.
Reopen the dashboard and verify Auto-apply filters remains disabled.
Choose More > Duplicate, enter a new name, and confirm Duplicate. Reproduce with either the default questions-copy mode or Only duplicate dashboard.
On the copied dashboard, open More > Edit settings. Observe Auto-apply filters is enabled.
Change a filter on the copy: queries execute immediately instead of waiting for Apply as they do on the source.

bugs.name: Reverting dashboard history leaves a deleted tab selected and hides restored content
bugs.summary: Reverting to a revision before the currently selected tab existed leaves no surviving tab selected. The dashboard falsely displays 'There's nothing here, yet' until a user manually selects an existing tab. Reproduced twice on dashboard8.
bugs.expected: When a history revert removes the active tab, the dashboard selects a surviving tab and displays its restored cards.
bugs.actual: Surviving tabs remain visible but none is selected; the dashboard displays 'There's nothing here, yet' with no grids. Clicking Tab 1 immediately restores its existing charts.
reproSteps: Sign in and open a saved dashboard with charts on Tab 1 and a history revision, such as /dashboard/8.
Enter Edit mode, create a new tab, add a heading such as QA Revert, and Save while the new tab is selected.
Click the Edited… history control and open History.
Revert to a revision from before the new tab existed (the reproduced entry on dashboard8 was 'You untrashed this Dashboard').
Close the info/history panel and wait for the restored dashboard to settle.
Observe that the remaining tabs are visible but no tab is selected, and the page says 'There's nothing here, yet'.
Click Tab 1; its restored charts appear, proving the empty state was incorrect.

bugs.name: Empty URL parameter bypasses a required dashboard filter
bugs.summary: An empty URL value clears a dashboard filter configured with a default and Always require a value, allowing its mapped question to return unfiltered data.
bugs.expected: A dashboard filter configured as required should keep a valid selection or prevent its mapped question from running without one; an empty URL parameter should not clear it and run unfiltered.
bugs.actual: A Region filter with default us-east and Always require a value returns two rows normally. Loading the dashboard with region= leaves the required filter blank and its mapped question returns all six rows, including in the public dashboard.
reproSteps: Create a dashboard with a question containing rows from multiple regions; add a Region filter and map it to the question.
Set default Region to us-east and enable Always require a value. Save the dashboard.
Open the saved dashboard and confirm Region shows us-east and the mapped question returns the two matching seeded rows.
Load the same dashboard URL with an empty region query parameter (region=), keeping other parameters unchanged. Wait for the page to settle.
Observe the Region chip is blank and the mapped question returns all six seeded rows; the required setting remains enabled.
If public sharing is available, open the public dashboard and repeat the control and empty-parameter navigations; observe the same two-to-six row change.

bugs.name: Mapping a multi-value filter to a SQL text variable keeps the extra values and breaks the card
bugs.summary: Mapping a multi-value filter to a SQL text variable keeps the extra values and breaks the card.
bugs.expected: Mapping the Region filter to the card should filter the card and display results.
bugs.actual: With two Region values selected, map the dashboard filter to a SQL question's plain text variable and save. Metabase silently switches the filter to "A single value" and the chip shows one value, but the card query still sends both and the card shows "There was a problem displaying this chart." One selected value works (control).
reproSteps: Duplicate seeded Release overview dashboard using Only duplicate the dashboard and a unique QA name.
Edit the copy. Add Text or Category filter Region (Is), map Release requests table to Region, save. Select us-east and us-west and apply.
Edit copy, add Tab 2 and add existing saved question Release requests by region and category; save. The new card displays six rows before mapping.
Edit, select Region filter on Tab 2, choose Region in the card's Column to filter on dropdown. The settings automatically change from Dropdown list/Multiple values to Input box/A single value.
Click Done and Save.

bugs.name: Dashboard After or Before date filters ignore the selected time
bugs.summary: Dashboard After or Before date filters ignore the selected time.
bugs.expected: After October 17 2026 7:34 PM includes ID4, created at 7:35 PM that day, along with IDs5 and 6.
bugs.actual: A dashboard Date filter set to After <date> <time> (e.g. After Oct 17 9:38 PM) hides rows later that same day. The chip and URL keep the time, but the SQL uses created_at >= the next midnight. On, Between, question-builder and native SQL filters keep minute precision (controls).
reproSteps: Open seed2 Release overview. Duplicate with a fresh QA-Date-prefixed name and check Only duplicate the dashboard.
Edit duplicate, Add a filter or parameter > Date picker. Map Release requests to Created At; Done and Save.
Open Date > Fixed date range > On. Set October 17, 2026, Add time, enter 19:35 (7:35 PM), and apply. Observe ID4 dated October17 7:35 PM.
Reopen Date, choose After, change time to 19:34 (7:34 PM), and Update filter.

bugs.name: Discarding a filter default edit keeps the canceled value applied and remembers it
bugs.summary: Discarding a filter default edit keeps the canceled value applied and remembers it.
bugs.expected: Discarding changes restores the dashboard to its prior Month grouping rather than applying the canceled Day grouping.
bugs.actual: Change a filter default in edit mode, then Cancel → Discard changes. The canceled value stays applied and is saved as your last-used value, so it returns on fresh visits. The saved default is unchanged.
reproSteps: Dashboards-only. Do not edit underlying questions or seed dashboard. Observed duplicate dashboard/31; create a fresh equivalent duplicate.
Open seed1 E-commerce Insights dashboard; use its menu Duplicate, give a fresh QA-Date2-prefixed name and check Only duplicate the dashboard.
Edit the duplicate, select Date Grouping, set Default value to Month, click Done and Save. Reopen the dashboard without query parameters to verify Month and monthly chart.
Edit Date Grouping again; change Default value from Month to Day.
Click dashboard Cancel, then Discard changes in the confirmation dialog.
Inspect the dashboard grouping and charts.

bugs.name: Re-clicking the selected Between tab rewrites the date range
bugs.summary: Re-clicking the selected Between tab rewrites the date range.
bugs.expected: Clicking the selected Between tab preserves March 2 and March 3 bounds in the editor.
bugs.actual: With a dashboard Date Range filter applied as March 2–3, reopen it and click the already-selected Between tab. The fields change to January 31 – March 2 while the chip and calendar highlight still show March 2–3. Clicking another tab and back, or not clicking, keeps the range (control).
reproSteps: Observed on own dashboard/31. Fresh equivalent setup requested; Dashboards only. This followed Date Grouping restriction to Day/Week and switching Day to Week; uncertain whether grouping restriction is necessary.
Duplicate seed1 E-commerce Insights with Only duplicate the dashboard checked and a fresh QA-Date2-prefixed name.
Set Date Range Between March 2, 2026 and March 3, 2026 and apply.
Edit Date Grouping options to only Day and Week, save, then select Day. Refresh and select Week.
Open Date Range and click its already selected Between tab.
Compare Start/End editor fields against applied range chip and highlighted calendar dates.

bugs.name: Required dashboard filter mapped to a SQL variable can be cleared from its text input
bugs.summary: Required dashboard filter mapped to a SQL variable can be cleared from its text input.
bugs.expected: A required filter should never be empty. Clearing it should either keep the previous value or reset it to the default, Documentation, so the category predicate stays applied.
bugs.actual: A required dashboard filter (with a default) mapped to a SQL text variable renders as an inline input. Clear it (Ctrl+A, Backspace) and press Enter, Tab or click away: the URL becomes category= and the card shows all rows. Popover widgets, a blur on an already-empty input, and the saved SQL question all restore the default (controls).
reproSteps: As an admin, duplicate the Release overview dashboard with Only duplicate the dashboard checked, and edit the copy.
Add the saved SQL question Release requests by region and category. Add a Text or Category filter and map it only to that card's Category variable.
Set the filter to Input box, A single value, default Documentation, and Always require a value. Save. The filter shows as an inline text box and the card shows the Documentation rows.
Type Infrastructure in the filter and press Enter. The card filters to Infrastructure.
Click the filter, select all, press Backspace, then press Enter.
Observe the filter is empty, the URL has the filter parameter with no value, and the card shows all rows. Refresh: the filter stays empty and all rows still show.

bugs.name: Deleting the initially selected dashboard tab leaves no tab selected and hides the remaining tab's cards
bugs.summary: Deleting the initially selected dashboard tab leaves no tab selected and hides the remaining tab's cards.
bugs.expected: After deleting the active tab, select a remaining tab and display its existing content rather than showing the dashboard creation empty state.
bugs.actual: Delete the tab that was selected on load (URL ?tab= or default) before clicking any tab. No tab ends up selected and the dashboard shows the empty state while the remaining tab still has cards. Clicking a tab first works (control).
reproSteps: Dashboard 25 is an owned disposable fixture. Do not modify seeded dashboards or questions. Fresh two-tab fixture with saved content in both tabs is sufficient to test equivalent behavior.
Create a fresh QA-prefixed dashboard with two tabs named QA Source and QA Target.

Add text and a link to each tab; save and reload to verify both tabs contain their distinct content. Observed fixture had QA Source text “QA copied text — independent target 2026” plus a dashboard link.
Select second tab QA Target, enter Edit dashboard, open its tab dropdown and choose Delete.
Observe remaining QA Source tab and dashboard canvas without selecting another tab.

bugs.name: Browser Back to a deleted dashboard tab shows an empty dashboard with no tab selected
bugs.summary: Browser Back to a deleted dashboard tab shows an empty dashboard with no tab selected.
bugs.expected: Going back in browser history to a tab that was deleted falls back to an existing tab or says the tab is gone.
bugs.actual: After deleting a previously visited tab and saving, browser Back leaves no tab selected and shows There's nothing here, yet with Add a chart, although the remaining tabs have content.
reproSteps: Duplicate a dashboard that has several populated tabs.
Create an empty tab, save, and visit that tab.
Return to the first tab, edit the dashboard, delete the visited tab, and save.
Press browser Back and observe no tab is selected and the empty-dashboard placeholder shows.

bugs.name: Fixed date range picker overflows the viewport on phones
bugs.summary: Fixed date range picker overflows the viewport on phones.
bugs.expected: The date filter picker should fit the mobile viewport so both date fields and the confirmation control are visible.
bugs.actual: At phone width (390px), open a dashboard date filter → Fixed date range → Between. The two-calendar picker renders ~634px wide; the end date is clipped, Add filter sits off the right edge, and the page scrolls horizontally. Fits at 640px and wider; Before/On/After fit at 390 (controls).
reproSteps: Sign in and open /dashboard/1.
Set the browser viewport to 390×844 (or use a narrow mobile-sized window).
Click Date Range, then Fixed date range….
Observe the clipped end date/calendar and missing confirmation button at the right edge; horizontal page scrolling is required to reach them.

bugs.name: Between number filter cannot be corrected from reversed bounds because Update filter stays disabled
bugs.summary: Between number filter cannot be corrected from reversed bounds because Update filter stays disabled.
bugs.expected: The 'Update filter' button remains enabled so the updated range from 100 to 300 can be submitted.
bugs.actual: Apply a Between number filter with reversed bounds (300, 100): No results, as expected. Reopen it and fix the order to 100, 300: Update filter stays disabled and Enter does nothing, so the empty dashboard can't be corrected. Any non-permuted change (100, 301) works (control).
reproSteps: Duplicate Release overview via dashboard menu; use a unique QA-Filter name and check Only duplicate the dashboard.
Edit owned copy; add Text or Category filter named Region, map Release requests to Region, save; select us-east and us-west and apply.
Edit owned copy; add Number filter named Amount, map Release requests to Amount, choose Between operator, save.
Set Amount range 120 to 240 and apply; verify rows 1 and 2. Change to 120.5 to 240.5 and apply; verify only row 2.
Change Amount to 300 to 100 and apply; dashboard shows No results. Refresh and reopen Amount.
Correct first endpoint to 100 and second to 300. Attempt Update filter.

bugs.name: Center-aligned text card leaves Markdown bullet markers at the left edge
bugs.summary: Center-aligned text card leaves Markdown bullet markers at the left edge.
bugs.expected: With Horizontal Alignment set to Center, list bullets stay next to their item text.
bugs.actual: The list item text is centered while the bullet markers stay at the left edge of the card.
reproSteps: Edit a dashboard and add a Text card with a heading and two bullet list items.
Open the card's visualization options and set Horizontal Alignment to Center.
Save and observe the bullets are detached from the centered text.

bugs.name: Bottom- or middle-aligned text cards hide overflowing content above the scroll area
bugs.summary: Bottom- or middle-aligned text cards hide overflowing content above the scroll area.
bugs.expected: All text remains readable by scrolling within the card; when content exceeds card height, alignment should not put it outside the scrollable bounds.
bugs.actual: A dashboard text card with more content than fits, set to Vertical Alignment Bottom, shows only the end of its text. The heading and list sit above the scroll area and can't be scrolled to. The same card set to Top scrolls through everything; a taller Bottom card shows all content (controls).
reproSteps: From /collection/root, create a new dashboard. Add a Text card.

Enter this multiline Markdown: “# Text dashboard”, a blank line, “- First item”, “- Second item”, a blank line, “[Internal link](/dashboard/2)”, a blank line, “| Name | Value |”, “|---|---|”, and “| Test | 42 |”. Keep the default short text-card height.
Open the text card’s Show visualization options. Set Vertical Alignment to Bottom, click Done, and save the dashboard.
Reload and try to read the beginning of the card by scrolling. The heading and list are inaccessible; only the final content is visible.
As a control, change Vertical Alignment to Top: the heading appears and the card provides a scrollbar for the rest.

bugs.name: Cancel does not undo Reset to defaults in dashboard card visualization settings
bugs.summary: Cancel does not undo Reset to defaults in dashboard card visualization settings.
bugs.expected: Clicking Cancel should discard the reset and preserve the previously saved table formatting and pagination settings.
bugs.actual: In dashboard edit mode, open a card's visualization settings, click Reset to defaults, then Cancel (or Escape). The card loses its conditional formatting, pagination and custom title anyway. Other edits made in the same modal are discarded by Cancel (control).
reproSteps: Create an isolated dashboard copy of Release overview with an existing Release requests table; do not alter the seed or question.

Edit the table visualization: enable pagination and add whole-row Region = us-east blue and Amount > 200 green conditional rules. Save visualization and dashboard, then refresh to verify colors and pagination.
Edit dashboard, open Release requests visualization options, click Reset to defaults, then Cancel.
Observe the card and reopen visualization options.

bugs.name: Changing a dashboard card's visualization settings resets its click behavior to drill-through
bugs.summary: Changing a dashboard card's visualization settings resets its click behavior to drill-through.
bugs.expected: Changing a card's display settings, such as Show total or its title, keeps the card's configured click behavior.
bugs.actual: A donut card set to Update a dashboard filter on click reverts to Open the drill-through menu after a visualization setting is changed and saved.
reproSteps: Duplicate a dashboard with a donut chart card.
Edit the card's click behavior to Update a dashboard filter and map a column to a filter; save.
Edit the dashboard, open the card's visualization settings, change Show total, and save.
Reopen click behavior and observe it is back to the drill-through menu.

bugs.name: Whitespace-only inline dashboard rename leaves a blank title with no error
bugs.summary: Whitespace-only inline dashboard rename leaves a blank title with no error.
bugs.expected: An invalid whitespace-only rename should immediately retain/revert to the last saved name or display validation, rather than leaving an apparently updated blank dashboard title.
bugs.actual: Rename a dashboard inline to only spaces and click away (or press Enter). The title goes blank with no error; the server rejected the save (400) and a reload restores the old name. An empty rename reverts correctly and valid renames save (controls).
reproSteps: Use a fresh owned dashboard; do not mutate shared seeds or questions. This is a missing invalid-input recovery/feedback issue, not a claim that blank names persist.
As Harbor Admin create a fresh disposable dashboard with a nonblank name, or duplicate a seeded dashboard into your own fixture. Observed fixture was dashboard 30 named QA-Life2 SearchRenamed-2030.
In saved view click the editable dashboard title and replace its entire contents with three spaces.
Click a dashboard content heading outside the title and wait for the settled state.
Observe blank title and no validation; reload the dashboard and compare.

bugs.name: Opening a permanently deleted dashboard from trash search shows a not-found page
bugs.summary: Opening a permanently deleted dashboard from trash search shows a not-found page.
bugs.expected: A dashboard search result opens the dashboard or its trash page, and permanently deleted items no longer appear.
bugs.actual: After permanently deleting a dashboard, searching with Search items in trash still lists it, and clicking the result opens the page-not-found screen.
reproSteps: Create a dashboard with a unique name and save it.
Move it to Trash, then delete it permanently from Trash.
Search for its name, open View and filter all results, and enable Search items in trash.
Click the dashboard result and observe the not-found page.

bugs.name: Sample dashboard History shows undefined as the author
bugs.summary: Sample dashboard History shows undefined as the author.
bugs.expected: Every dashboard History entry names who made the change.
bugs.actual: On the sample E-commerce Insights dashboard, More info > History shows undefined modified this. A newly created dashboard shows You created this.
reproSteps: Open the sample E-commerce Insights dashboard.
Open More info > History.
Observe the entry reads undefined modified this.

bugs.name: Discarding a filter removal restores the filter but clears its active value
bugs.summary: Discarding a filter removal restores the filter but clears its active value.
bugs.expected: Discard changes should restore both the removed filter definition and its previous active selection, leaving the view unchanged.
bugs.actual: A fresh dashboard copy filtered Release requests Category to Documentation showed three rows IDs1,3,5 and text=Documentation in the URL. After Edit > remove Text > Cancel > Discard changes, Text reappeared empty, URL became text=, and all six rows including Infrastructure were displayed. Reproduced on three fresh dashboards.
reproSteps: Sign in, open /dashboard/2, and duplicate it with Only duplicate the dashboard enabled.
Edit the copy and add a Text or Category filter. Map it to Release requests > Category, then Done and Save.
In view mode select Documentation in the Text filter and click Add filter. Confirm three rows remain.
Click Edit dashboard, click the Text filter, and choose Remove.
Click the top Cancel button, then Discard changes.
Observe that Text returns with no selected value and the table now shows all six rows.

bugs.name: Duplicating a card drops its local filter default and required-value setting
bugs.summary: Duplicating a card drops its local filter default and required-value setting.
bugs.expected: A duplicated card should retain its local filter configuration, including default values and Always require a value, and initially display the same filtered data.
bugs.actual: A Release requests card with a card-local Number Between Amount filter defaulted to 100–200 and required enabled duplicates with Number 1 set to No default and required disabled. The copy consequently displays rows outside the source's range (Amount 360 appeared alongside 120 in the tested Region subset). Reproduced twice.
reproSteps: Sign in, open /dashboard/2, and use Move, trash, and more… > Duplicate with Only duplicate the dashboard checked to create a test copy.
Edit the copy. Add a filter or parameter > Number > Between, and map it to Release requests > Amount.
Set its default range to 100 and 200, enable Always require a value, and move the filter onto the Release requests card. Click Done and Save.
Re-enter Edit dashboard, hover the Release requests card, choose Duplicate, and Save.
Compare the original and duplicated card data and local filters. Open the copied filter's editor: its default is missing and Always require a value is off.

bugs.name: Duplicating a tab loses text-card variable mappings
bugs.summary: Duplicating a tab loses text-card variable mappings.
bugs.expected: Copied text cards should retain their mapped variables and display the same filter values as the original tab.
bugs.actual: A fresh dashboard contained Heading {{region}} and Text {{region}}, both mapped to a heading-local Region input filter default West, required enabled. Original rendered Heading West and Text West. Duplicating Tab1 produced Heading West but Text {{region}} in Copy of Tab1, persisting after full reload. Changing filter values on a second mixed dashboard similarly updated the copied heading but left copied text literal, while original text interpolated correctly.
reproSteps: Sign in and create a new dashboard from /collection/root > New > Dashboard.
Add a heading card with Heading {{region}}.
Hover the heading, click Add a filter > Text or Category. Map its variable selector to region, label the filter Region, and choose Input box.
Set default West and enable Always require a value, then Done.
Add a text card with Text {{region}}. Click the heading's Region widget in Edit, map the text card's Select variable control to region, then Done and Save.
Verify both cards display West.
Edit dashboard, open Tab 1's dropdown, choose Duplicate, and Save.
View Copy of Tab 1 and reload: heading displays West, but the text displays literal {{region}}.

bugs.name: Editing a copied tab's card-local filter jumps to the original tab
bugs.summary: Editing a copied tab's card-local filter jumps to the original tab.
bugs.expected: Clicking a card-local filter on the copied tab should keep that tab selected and configure the copied heading's filter.
bugs.actual: With Copy of Tab 1 selected in dashboard edit mode, clicking its heading's Text widget switches selection and URL to source Tab 1 and opens settings there. Reproduced on a fresh dashboard and reconfirmed after fresh navigation. fresh-navigation snapshots 16:57:44 and 16:57:49 show dashboard3 tab=24-copy-of-tab-1 switching to tab=10-tab-1.
reproSteps: From /collection/root, choose New > Dashboard, enter a unique name, and Create.
Add a heading containing “Region {{region}}”. Hover the heading and choose Add a filter > Text or Category.
In the heading's Select… mapping choose region; set How should people filter to Input box, then Done and Save.
Edit the dashboard. Open Tab 1's chevron menu and choose Duplicate, then Save.
Edit again and select Copy of Tab 1.
Click the copied heading's Text widget. Observe that selection jumps to source Tab 1 and filter settings open there.

bugs.name: Dashboard More info "Creator and last editor" omits creator row for Harbor Admin-created dashboard viewed by Maya
bugs.summary: Dashboard More info "Creator and last editor" omits creator row for Harbor Admin-created dashboard viewed by Maya.
bugs.expected: The Creator and last editor card names Harbor Admin as the creator and Maya Chen as the last editor.
bugs.actual: The card shows only the last-editor row for Maya Chen. No creator row appears, even though History lists "Harbor Admin created this."

Sign in as Maya (Member).
As Maya, open that dashboard and click More info (i). Change the description to 'Maya noncreator member edit checkpoint' and blur the field to save.
Refresh the page, click More info (i) and look at the Overview tab's 'Creator and last editor' card. It shows only the last-editor row for Maya Chen.
Open the History tab. It shows 'Harbor Admin created this.'

bugs.name: Opening an internal link card’s editor corrupts its destination when saved
bugs.summary: Opening an internal link card’s editor corrupts its destination when saved.
bugs.expected: Opening the link editor and saving an unchanged card should preserve the selected dashboard target.
bugs.actual: A link selected from search initially points to /dashboard/2-release-overview. After opening its pencil editor and saving without edits, the href becomes literal 'Release overview'. It persists after reload, and clicking navigates to /Release%20overview with 'We're a little lost… The page you asked for couldn't be found.' Independently reproduced on dashboards4 and12.
reproSteps: Sign in and create a new dashboard through /collection/root > New > Dashboard.
In the editor choose Add a link or iframe > Link.
Type Release overview and select the existing dashboard from the search results. Save the dashboard.
Verify the link card opens or points to /dashboard/2-release-overview, then return to the test dashboard.
Click Edit dashboard, hover the internal link card, and click its pencil editor.
Without changing the input or selecting another result, click the dashboard Save button.
Reload and click the link card. It navigates to /Release%20overview and shows a not-found page.

bugs.name: Valid upper-only Between filter reverses to lower-only after reload
bugs.summary: A Between filter with only an upper bound (for example when the lower bound was left blank or was invalid text like abc) changes after reload: the upper value moves into the lower field, so the filter becomes lower-only.
bugs.expected: Accepted upper-only range remains Amount <=240 after reload, retaining IDs 2 and 6.
bugs.actual: Reload changes results to IDs 2 and 4 (240 and 360), interpreting 240 as the lower bound instead. No invalid text was entered in this reproduction.
reproSteps: Create a dashboard with the Release requests card, a Number Between filter mapped to Amount, and a Boolean Approved filter set to False.
Open Amount; leave first bound empty and enter 240 in second bound. Add filter is enabled; apply it.
Observe Release requests IDs 2 and 6, amounts 240 and 150.
Reload the dashboard and inspect the same card.

matchingGuidance.claimScope: Credit any Between filter whose upper bound moves into the lower field after reload, whatever the reason the lower bound was empty, including invalid non-numeric input. Non-numeric input that clears a filter without the bound moving is a separate known-invalid reference.

bugs.name: Trashed empty dashboards still offer Add a chart, leading to a permission error on Save
bugs.summary: Trashed empty dashboards still offer Add a chart, leading to a permission error on Save.

reviewEvidence.basis: Fresh targeted browser reproduction under delegated reviewer judgment.
reviewEvidence.analysis: The seeded dashboard revision response has no timestamp.
